'''Suzu no Gozen''' (鈴之御前社) is a Shinto shrine located in Aichi Prefecture, Nagoya, Atsuta Ward.

It is a subsidiary shrine (Massha) of Atsuta Shrine, with its enshrined deity being Ame-no-Uzume. Locally, it is colloquially known as "Suzu no Miya" (鈴の宮). In the past, a river known as Shōjin River flowed near the shrine, and travelers along the Tōkaidō were required to receive a bell purification ritual at this shrine to cleanse themselves before visiting Atsuta.

After the war, it was relocated (Sengū) to its current site facing the former Tōkaidō.

From the subway station Atsuta Shrine Denmachō Station, if you proceed about 50 m to the southwest, you will reach the former Tōkaidō road. Continuing approximately 100 m toward the southeast, the shrine grounds will appear on your right. The grounds are only a few meters wide and are hard to spot from the national road.

== Annual Festival ==
Every year on July 31, the shrine is known for its Summer Purification (commonly known as the "Passing Through the Straw Ring" ritual).
